daily_brief: The UN General Assembly dominated global headlines today as President Trump threatened to 'annihilate' Iran before US and Iranian officials held their first talks since a June ceasefire collapsed [BBC], [Al Jazeera]. The meeting, mediated by Qatar, produced no breakthrough but was described as 'constructive' by US envoy Steve Witkoff. Separately, the US, Denmark, and Greenland signed a defence deal allowing Washington to build two new military bases in the Arctic territory, defusing over a year of tension sparked by Trump's earlier threats to 'take' the island [BBC], [The Economist]. Chinese President Xi Jinping departed Beijing for Washington ahead of his second summit with Trump this year, with Taiwan arms sales and trade tensions on the agenda [Nikkei Asia], [France 24]. In Europe, Ukraine expressed anger after the EU agreed to remove sanctions on Russian oligarchs Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman, with Kyiv calling the move 'unacceptable' [BBC]. Meanwhile, AI governance emerged as a key theme at the UNGA, with Trump rejecting international guardrails while AI pioneer Yoshua Bengio urged urgent global cooperation [ABC Australia], [France 24].

top_stories.headline: US and Iran Hold First Talks Since June as Trump Threatens 'Annihilation'
bullets: US and Iranian officials met on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, mediated by Qatar—their first talks since a June ceasefire unravelled.
President Trump, in his UNGA address, said he could 'annihilate' Iran if the conflict went unresolved; Iran's military warned of 'crushing' retaliation.
US envoy Steve Witkoff described the discussions as 'constructive and promising,' while Iran repeated its demand for the US to end 'acts of aggression.'
The Strait of Hormuz remains blocked following February's US-Israeli strikes on Iran, causing ongoing global oil price volatility.

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Focused on diplomatic process and Trump's domestic political pressures ahead of midterms.

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Emphasized escalatory rhetoric from both sides and Iran's military response.

sources.name: Le Monde
sources.framing_note: Headline noted Trump 'feigns hesitation' between deal and annihilation.

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Highlighted Iranian President Pezeshkian's upcoming UN address as key response.

top_stories.headline: US, Denmark, and Greenland Sign Defence Deal for Two New Military Bases
bullets: The three parties signed an agreement at the UNGA allowing the US to build military bases at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig in Greenland.
The deal reaffirms Danish sovereignty over the Arctic territory, ending over a year of tension after Trump threatened to 'take' Greenland.
Danish PM Mette Frederiksen called the deal 'good for the US, Denmark, Greenland, Europe and NATO'; Greenland's PM called it a 'win-win-win.'
The agreement updates the 1951 US-Denmark defence pact and addresses strategic concerns over Arctic defence and mineral resources.

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Straightforward diplomatic reporting on the signing and its significance.

sources.name: The Economist
sources.framing_note: Noted the deal is a 'modest improvement' but argued Trump's annexation threats were a 'costly blunder' that damaged transatlantic relations.

top_stories.headline: Xi Jinping Travels to Washington for Second Summit with Trump
bullets: Chinese President Xi Jinping departed Beijing for a three-day state visit to the US, accompanied by Foreign Minister Wang Yi and other senior officials.
The summit comes as a trade truce is set to expire in November, with tariffs, rare earth materials, and AI among key discussion topics.
Taiwan is watching closely; Trump previously described US arms sales to the island as a 'very good negotiating chip' with China.
Expectations for concrete outcomes are modest after the May Beijing summit produced largely symbolic results.

sources.name: Nikkei Asia
sources.framing_note: Detailed coverage of summit logistics, trade stakes, and Taiwan concerns.

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Brief mention in liveblog format alongside UNGA coverage.

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Focused on Taiwan's perspective and concerns over US arms sales.

top_stories.headline: EU Removes Sanctions on Two Russian Oligarchs, Sparking Ukrainian Anger
bullets: The EU agreed to remove sanctions on Russian-Uzbek billionaire Alisher Usmanov and Russian-Israeli businessman Mikhail Fridman, imposed after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
France advocated for Usmanov's removal citing 'national security concerns'; Luxembourg pushed for Fridman's delisting amid his lawsuit for frozen assets.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha called the decision 'unacceptable,' saying Moscow would see it as 'a sense of impunity' and 'humiliation of the EU.'
As part of a compromise, sanctions on nearly 3,000 other individuals and entities were extended for three years; Latvia announced it would impose national sanctions on both oligarchs.

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Balanced coverage including Ukrainian criticism and Kremlin response.

sources.name: Le Monde
sources.framing_note: Headline linked the pardoning of a jailed Frenchman in Azerbaijan to the sanctions decision.

sources.name: Financial Times
sources.framing_note: Described it as part of a 'secret prisoner release deal' (article behind paywall).

top_stories.headline: AI Pioneer Warns of Risks as Trump Rejects International Guardrails at UN
bullets: President Trump labeled concerns about AI 'a hoax' in his UNGA speech and rejected a joint statement from 22 countries, including Australia, calling for humans to remain in control of AI.
Professor Yoshua Bengio, co-chair of the UN Scientific Panel on AI and Turing Award winner, pushed back, calling for urgent international agreement on safeguards.
Bengio warned that decisions about AI's future 'shouldn't be the decisions of just a few CEOs or a few governments' and called for keeping 'human dignity flourishing at the centre.'
France announced an €80 million plan to boost AI skills in the workplace, noting French companies lag behind other European economies in AI adoption.

sources.name: ABC Australia
sources.framing_note: Featured Bengio's direct rebuttal to Trump and emphasized urgency of global cooperation.

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Noted AI as taking 'centre stage' at UNGA with UK PM Andy Burnham among leaders addressing it.

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Focused on France's domestic AI skills initiative rather than UNGA debate.
